name: particle-breath
summary: Full-bleed dark section with a soft, folded volume of 8500 dots breathing slowly in the middle of the frame. The dots are fixed samples on a sphere that never re-scatter; each frame a ripple, a diagonal saddle fold and a twist deform the same points, twelve depth buckets fade the back of the volume, and a few strays orbit just off the surface. Canvas 2D, no WebGL, no dependencies. Under reduced motion it holds a still frame, as upstream's own demo does.

backgroundColor.description: Canvas ground. Set --fx-bg to match so the CSS resting state agrees.

scale.description: Size of the volume, in percent of upstream's default.

particleCount.description: How many particles sample the surface. Changing it re-samples them.

opacity.description: Opacity of the whole graphic over the ground, composited once so overlaps do not double up.

speed.description: Breathing speed. 0 holds a still frame.

breathStrength.description: How far the surface ripples and twists as it breathes.

deviations.what: src/geometry.js and src/index.js are pasted into one module, geometry first, with their import and export lines removed. The functions are upstream's, unchanged.
deviations.why: Seam. An item ships one index.js and no sibling modules, and the repo contract exports only mount and meta.

deviations.what: mount() creates the canvas inside the section and drives upstream's own mountParticleBreath() with a config provider, which is upstream's live-controls API. update() merges into the object that provider returns; destroy() calls upstream's returned stop function, removes the canvas and clears data-fx-live.
deviations.why: Seam. The repo contract is mount(el, opts) returning { update, destroy }, and upstream already has exactly that shape.

deviations.what: An IntersectionObserver stops upstream's loop when the section leaves the viewport and starts a fresh one when it returns, so the breathing clock restarts from zero off screen.
deviations.why: Ours. Upstream's loop never pauses, and a section nobody can see does not need 8500 particles a frame.

deviations.what: The provider sets data-fx-live on its second call, after the first frame has drawn, and a refused 2D context (upstream's throw) removes the canvas and returns the resting handle.
deviations.why: Ours. The CSS rest must not fade out from under an empty canvas, and a failed mount must leave the section finished.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion the provider returns speed 0, so the canvas holds upstream's frame at time zero instead of the section returning at once.
deviations.why: Upstream's own answer: examples/index.html passes speed 0 when reduced motion matches. The still frame is the effect at rest, which beats a CSS imitation of it.
